name: Basilica of Saint John the Evangelist
history: Irish immigrants founded the parish in the 1850s, worshipping in a small wooden church dedicated in 1851. The stone church was begun in 1868 and consecrated on 30 May 1886, then the largest in Connecticut. Benedict XVI named it a basilica in 2009.
arch: A Gothic Revival stone church by James Murphy of Providence, who designed fifty-six Catholic churches across New England; its interior was designed by Dublin theatre designer John Ennis. A tall square tower rises beside the nave.
features: It is known as "the Mother Church of Stamford".
The parish funded most of St. Joseph's Hospital, open from 1942 to 1999.

look.d: A square Gothic tower with pinnacles marks the mother church of Stamford.
The basilica is especially known for its Solemn Mass.

fun: The city named three affordable housing towers "Saint John's Towers" after the parish.
journal: Irish immigrants' stone church, once the largest in Connecticut.

a: A Dublin theatre designer, John Ennis
